answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The ledge multiplier is published, charged in terrace, and bridge lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2141 identities would post 1134 proofs and burn roughly 37 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
